title: Private VPC upgrade: connection-queue surge on agent nvme socket — mitigation & follow-up
creator: Maya Patel
description: During a staged Private/VPC control plane upgrade in us-west-2 we observed a sustained surge of queued control-plane connections on the agent side that caused excessive retry storms and degraded connectivity for ~18 minutes. Unlike prior conntrack/NAT regressions, the initial signal pointed at NVMe-backed local IPC socket write amplification causing internal driver backpressure and delayed accept() handling in the agent process. This ticket captures the investigation, temporary mitigations applied during the incident, root cause analysis, and assigned follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
impact: ~320 tenants with private clusters in the upgraded region experienced degraded control-plane RPC success rates (10-40% error spike) and elevated orchestration latencies. No customer data lost. Some Dedicated/Dedicated-like workloads hit autoscaler timeouts and rolled back deployments.

mitigation: Rollback control plane binary to v2026.02.28 for impacted canaries
Disable nvme_ipc_coalesce flag in agent config across paused region (feature-flag gated)
Apply backpressure thresholds in the agent accept loop to shed new connections instead of queuing indefinitely
Added circuit-breaker to orchestration controller to avoid infinite retrying of failing agent RPCs
root_cause: A performance regression introduced in v2026.03.05 enabled aggressive NVMe IPC write coalescing in the agent's local socket path. Under bursty upgrade traffic the kernel async write queue and the agent's epoll loop entered a pathological state where accept() and read callbacks were starved. This manifested as queue growth at the agent accept layer and subsequent orchestration retries. Contributing factors: insufficient observability on agent socket queue depth, no unit tests covering high-burst IPC patterns, and an unchecked interaction between new coalescing code and existing epoll edge-triggered handling.
